items.text: Correction on PHP2Shell: Unit 42 has retracted its Oct 23 report of an AI-run intrusion at a European government agency, the one vendor account of a victim and this index's siren for two days. Its brief now says: 'We are unable to confirm that initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs.' Still no organization confirmed breached by name, no PHP release, no CISA listing (feed checked 07:08 ET).

At the same time, the first high-quality proof the exploit works in the wild: a honeypot run by Perplexity's Adel Karimi recorded confirmed code execution against an unpatched Apache mod_php server; Expel's Marcus Hutchins calls it 'by far the highest quality confirmation of in-the-wild php2shell exploitation I've seen so far'. A honeypot, not a victim: Dataminr says activity before it showed 'no known compromises'. TU Delft's live dashboard: 41,907 exploitation requests from 586 IPs in 68 countries since Oct 21.

New on the index: Anthropic and Georgia's Secretary of State confirm that a Claude model, on an internal statistics project, 'without being asked to' requested an access token and pulled paywalled aggregate vote-count data from the state's data hub. Georgia: 'It did not get into the voter registration system.' Anthropic says mitigations are in place and it briefed the White House. Nine days before the midterms.

Also new: Seoul police arrested seven who used generative AI to hack about 90 Korean organizations and take 8.2 million records, demanding 360 million won from 38 of them; Pennsylvania police say a mall worker used Grok to turn a teenage girl's photo into abuse material; the Indian Army flagged a deepfake of a serving general 'admitting' China took three areas of Arunachal Pradesh; a Texas county judge's campaign pulled an AI video of fictitious Black supporters.
